assumptions: The continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio, and PID computations are treated as external plant/controller dynamics; the discrete FSM consumes the resulting slip-error input `slp`.
The initial state is `increase` because no explicit initial state was provided and `increase` is the first named FSM state in the natural-language description.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: single-wheel ABS hydraulic regulator as a three-state FSM
transition guards split the slip-error space into four bands using `slp`

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: first empty cycle dispatches initial transition to increase and applies inlet-valve command k1=1,k2=0,n=0.
scenario_results.name: default_init_enters_increase_outputs

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: increase must transition to hold exactly at slp=0.01 and neutralize valves.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire probe: increase must remain increase when slp is just above 0.01.
scenario_results.name: increase_no_fire_above_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: hold must transition to increase when slp is greater than 0.01 and set inlet-valve command.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire probe: hold must not transition to increase at exactly slp=0.01 because the guard is strict greater-than.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_fire_at_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: hold must transition to decrease when slp is less than -0.01 and command pressure release k2=1,n=500.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire probe: hold must not transition to decrease at exactly slp=-0.01 because the guard is strict less-than.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_fire_at_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: decrease must transition to hold exactly at slp=-0.01 and neutralize valves and pump.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_lower_boundary

evidence: NL: FSM contains states `increase`, `hold`, and `decrease`.
DSL: `state increase`, `state hold`, `state decrease` under `ABSHydraulicRegulator`.
NL/DSL match: increase sets `k1=1, k2=0, n=0`; hold sets `k1=0, k2=0, n=0`; decrease sets `k1=0, k2=1, n=500`.
NL/DSL match: guards `slp <= 0.01`, `slp > 0.01`, `slp < -0.01`, and `slp >= -0.01` are represented exactly.
findings.summary: The DSL faithfully captures the NL-specified three-state hydraulic supervisor, including state names, initial entry into increase, per-state valve/pump assignments, and the four slip-error transition guards.

evidence: inspect metrics: `n_states_leaf=3`, `n_states_composite=1`, `n_variables=4`, `action_count=3`.
GroundingMap includes required elements for all states, variables, entry actions, transitions, and guards.
sim_summary: 8 scenarios passed, including boundary and no-fire probes for upper and lower thresholds.
findings.summary: Required discrete FSM components are covered: one composite regulator state, three leaf modes, four variables, three entry actions, and all four NL-required normal transitions.

evidence: NL: wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute the slip ratio, and PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor.
DSL: only declares `slp`, `k1`, `k2`, and `n`; no wheel speed, vehicle speed, slip computation, PID state, or controller equations are present.
GroundingMap assumption: continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio, and PID computations are treated as external plant/controller dynamics; the FSM consumes `slp`.
findings.summary: The PID, wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio computation, and plant dynamics are not modeled internally; they are abstracted into external input `slp`. This is acceptable for the discrete-supervisor scope but limits end-to-end ABS behavioral coverage.

evidence: design diagnostics: `W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR` for `slp`.
design diagnostics: `W_UNREFERENCED_VAR` for `k1`, `k2`, and `n`.
design diagnostics: `external_input_role_ledger` identifies `slp` as an external input candidate.
NL: the continuous wheel-slip dynamics remain in the plant model; discrete supervisor maps thresholds to valve and pump actions.
findings.summary: Diagnostics report `slp` as read but never written and output variables as unreferenced by guards. In this model these are mostly role-separation artifacts: `slp` is an external input and `k1`, `k2`, `n` are pure outputs.

evidence: Warnings are advisory only, with `blocking_count=0` and no warning budget exhaustion.
`slp` is intentionally consumed as an externally supplied slip-error/PID signal.
`k1`, `k2`, and `n` are actuator outputs, not supervisory decision inputs in the NL.
findings.summary: The advisory warnings should not be fixed by adding artificial writes to `slp` or by forcing output variables into guards, because that would reduce NL fidelity. A role annotation or interface distinction would be the safer remedy if the DSL supports it.

evidence: All required discrete states, guards, and actions from the NL are present.
design_diagnostics_summary.ok=true with `blocking_count=0`.
sim_summary.ok=true with 8/8 scenarios passed.
Remaining limitation is scope abstraction of continuous/PID dynamics rather than missing required FSM behavior.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate for the scoped discrete supervisor. No quality cap is warranted for the FSM itself, but the model should not be treated as a full ABS/PID/plant reference.

evidence: GroundingMap assumption explicitly externalizes continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio, and PID computations.
DSL contains only the discrete supervisor and actuator outputs.
five_component_summary is empty, so there is no additional FE/NGF/REC/GAS/SCB/AAT/BVS/DMR decomposition evidence beyond the provided grounding and simulation summaries.
findings.summary: The main residual quality risk comes from scope compression in the agent loop: mixed NL describing both continuous/PID dynamics and the discrete Stateflow supervisor was resolved by extracting only the supervisor and treating `slp` as an external input.

evidence: sim_summary: 8 scenarios passed.
Scenario set covers default initialization, upper-boundary transition behavior, lower-boundary transition behavior, and no-fire cases.
No simulation setup errors or runtime errors reported.
findings.summary: Path-1 evaluation risk is low for the scoped FSM because tests exercise all specified transitions, boundary cases, and entry outputs; risk remains only if evaluation expects full PID/plant behavior.
